A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRAB benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support matching retained material to the additions in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 20 LMMs, complexity and question-format analyses, evaluation-protocol comparisons, and appendix OCR experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds Real-task and GRAB-Lite evaluations, alternative performance metrics, and a plotting-library experiment.

M1.justification: The benchmark-generation pipeline gains screenshot compositing and image corruption, described in Appendix A, plus Seaborn regeneration of half the synthetic GRAB-Lite plots. These are limited construction-procedure extensions; the underlying graph-property generation, inference prompt, and core exact-matching procedure remain.

E1.justification: V3 adds the 1114-question Real task to the original four tasks: photographed paper and whiteboard drawings, graphs embedded in screenshots, and corrupted images. These introduce substantially different input conditions. GRAB-Lite mainly resamples the resulting five-task coverage rather than introducing another task.

E2.justification: The original 20-model comparison remains on the original tasks. V3 Table 6 adds 14 newer comparators against three retained models on GRAB-Lite, including GPT-5 variants, o1, newer Claude and Gemini models, and Grok 4. Table 4 also evaluates Gemini 2.0 Flash and 2.5 Flash on Real.

E3.justification: V3 introduces GRAB-Lite with 100 questions per task, approximate category/complexity balancing, mixed plotting libraries, and specified reasoning-effort settings. It also adds a paired 100-question plotting-library protocol and alternative metrics on Real Screenshots. The original exact-matching evaluation remains unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine performance across realistic image conditions, sensitivity to plotting-library appearance, and alternative performance metrics. The earlier complexity, answer-extraction, multiple-choice, and OCR analyses are retained; the multiple-choice analysis moves from v1 Section 4.7 to v3 Appendix B.

E5.justification: V3 Appendix C/Table 8 newly reports five-attempt pass@5 and 5/5 reliability for three models on Real Screenshots. This adds repeated-generation assessment without establishing increased repetitions of the original experiments. The existing 95% Wilson confidence intervals and general seed-setting statement are retained.

E6.justification: Original four-task, category, multiple-choice, and OCR scores are retained. Claude 3.5 Sonnet's overall score changes from 21.7% to 21.0% because GRAB now includes Real, not because of a same-setting decline. New results include GPT-5's 46.2% on GRAB-Lite and Claude 3.5 Sonnet's 30.0% versus 26.0% on Matplotlib versus Seaborn plots.

T1.justification: The greedy-decoding expression is retained, and neither version develops theoretical propositions or proofs. V3's additional empirical metrics do not introduce new formal definitions, derivations, or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the central contribution from an entirely synthetic four-task benchmark to a predominantly synthetic five-task benchmark with realistic inputs, accompanied by GRAB-Lite for costly reasoning models. The underlying claim that graph analysis remains challenging and supports straightforward exact-match evaluation is retained.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning robustness to noise and screenshot distractors, limited plotting-library effects, and a transformation-capability threshold crossed by newer models on GRAB-Lite. Appendix C also discusses the computational cost of repeated evaluation and limitations of distance-based metrics with varying answer scales and nonnumeric outputs.

D1.justification: New appendices document screenshot construction, corruption types, GRAB-Lite API routes and reasoning-effort settings, and additional model-version identifiers. The stated release expands to include generation code. The A100 inference estimate changes from about 30 to 45 minutes for the enlarged benchmark; hardware remains the same.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for newer evaluated models, Seaborn, and additional APIs, and motivates lightweight evaluation through inference-time reasoning costs. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing chart and multimodal benchmarks remain substantially unchanged; publication-metadata updates do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained, with localized condensation and terminology edits. Complexity and evaluation-protocol discussions are reordered, question-format analysis moves to the appendix, and appendix sections are reorganized around the added material. This is not an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 4 are redesigned to include Real examples, the statistics displays are reformatted, and the main results table is compressed and extended. V3 adds Real, GRAB-Lite, metric, and plotting-library tables plus Figure 7. Existing analysis figures are reordered and resized, including a changed evaluation-chart vertical scale.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially addresses v1's limited input realism and lack of economical evaluation for newer reasoning models through Real and GRAB-Lite, supported by additional validation and reproducibility details. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems: Section 4.3 retains a closed-model superiority claim contradicted by Table 3's GPT-4o mini 7.1% versus TransCore-M 7.9%, and Figure 7's purportedly equivalent Series examples do not match.
